full_text:
The NFL is into “Phase Three” of the offseason, which is the final stage before contact practices begin with training camp in late July. We’ve seen a steady stream of news since OTAs (organized team activities) started in mid-May, and it always gets a little more interesting in June when veteran players are required to report for one mandatory minicamp unless they have an excused absence.

I went team by team to round up the most important fantasy headlines coming out of all 32 workouts. I’ll update this article through June 18, the final day of team activities in Phase Three. Check back often for regular updates!

\>Each news item will have a date at the end of it for when it was updated or added to the article…ADP data used in this article is based on the last month of drafts with our partners over at [Underdog Fantasy](https://www.fantasypoints.com/underdog#/)…Subscribe to our [Fantasy Bundle Package](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans#/) to take your NFL research to the next level!

#### Cleveland Browns

+   The Browns are laying the early groundwork to name __Deshaun Watson__ as the Week 1 starter over __Shedeur Sanders__ once training camp rolls around. ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler [heard](https://x.com/ESPNCleveland/status/2056121255984566332?s=20) Watson has “hit it off with __Todd Monken__”, and Mary Kay Cabot [reported](https://x.com/MaryKayCabot/status/2049523640450871504?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet) in late April that Watson took the lead over Sanders. The decision to go with Watson is also another indication that Monken’s offense could be more of a spread attack than his TE-heavy attack in Baltimore. The Browns already selected __KC Concepcion__ and __Denzel Boston__ inside the top 39 picks to bolster their WR depth, and Watson previously struggled in __Kevin Stefanski__’s under-center offense. Watson is entering the final year of his disastrous five-year, $230 million contract he signed in 2022, and the Browns clearly want to take one final look at Watson since they’re paying him so much money. The Browns can also ice the Shedeur hype early in the season, but he’ll eventually get opportunities to play later in the season once Watson flames out. *(Added May 19)*

#### Pittsburgh Steelers

+   The Steelers and __Aaron Rodgers__ finally came to terms on a one-year, $22 million guaranteed deal that is worth up to $25 million. Rodgers wanted the ball out of his hands, finishing with the fastest average time to throw (2.38 seconds) and the fourth-lowest aDOT (6.3 yards) among 45 QBs who attempted 100+ passes. The style of play led him to rank 10th in catchable throw rate (76.9%) and fourth in turnover-worthy throw rate (1.6%), but 31st in hero throw rate (3.8%). He’s posted a solid 4.8% TD rate in each of his last three healthy campaigns, but he’s unlikely to do much better at 42 years old. The Steelers at least added __Michael Pittman__ and __Germie Bernard__ to a receiving corps that ranked 31st in 11 personnel (38.9%) under playcaller __Arthur Smith__. Rodgers will step into a familiar offense under his longtime Packers HC, __Mike McCarthy__, whose offense ranked ninth in 11 personnel (70.8%) in his final season with the Cowboys. Rodgers won two of his four MVPs under McCarthy, but those days are long gone. He should at least have a little more upside than his QB27 (14.7) from last season, with a better receiving corps around him. *(May 19)*

#### Kansas City Chiefs

+   __Rashee Rice__ is once again in trouble with the law. He triggered a 30-day jail sentence by testing positive for THC, which violated his five-year deferred probation for a third-degree felony charge last summer. He’ll miss Chiefs OTAs and mandatory minicamp while he serves jail time until June 16. He faced a six-game suspension to start last season for driving nearly 120 mph and causing a multi-car crash on a Dallas highway in March 2024. The NFL announced in early April that it closed its investigation into abuse allegations and that he wouldn’t face any additional discipline from the league. Rice’s career is on thin ice after his latest misstep, even if he doesn’t face an additional suspension for his latest legal issue. He could face a much longer jail sentence or have his probation revoked completely if he can’t stay out of his own way for the 4+ years remaining on his probation. Rice’s dynasty value takes another significant hit, and he’s a riskier pick for the upcoming season, especially if the Chiefs decide to protect themselves by signing a player like __Stefon Diggs__. *(Added May 19)*

#### Tampa Bay Buccaneers

+   GM __Jason Licht__ [said](https://www.tampabay.com/sports/bucs/2026/05/16/bucky-irving-kenneth-gainwell-sean-tucker-rachaad-white-zac-robinson/) __Bucky Irving__ would be limited during OTAs but should be ready for training camp. He suffered a left shoulder injury in Week 4 last season and missed seven straight games due to the issue and an ankle injury. He never regained his form even when he returned to the lineup, and he needed [offseason surgery](https://www.joebucsfan.com/2026/02/bucky-irving-had-offseason-shoulder-surgery/) to repair the lingering shoulder issue. Irving mentally struggled to get over his first major injury, so it shouldn’t be a huge surprise that the Buccaneers are taking it slow with Irving at this time of year. The Buccaneers paid __Kenneth Gainwell__ $9.83 million guaranteed to be a high-end #2 option behind Tampa Bay’s 2024 fourth-round pick. Gainwell has a history of earning a bigger role than expected, and this backfield is setting up to be a potential three-man committee. Bucky is a tough click for me at his current ADP (45, RB18) since he could be a between-the-20s player, with Gainwell stealing passing-game snaps and __Sean Tucker__ vulturing goal-line opportunities. *(Added May 19)*

__NFC West__
------------

#### Arizona Cardinals

+   __Jacoby Brissett__ wasn’t present for the start of Arizona’s voluntary OTAs as he seeks a pay raise on his $4.88 million contract, with just $1.5 million guaranteed for the 2026 season. He’s still being paid like a backup despite the organization informing him that he would open the season as the starter. Arizona handed __Gardner Minshew__ $5.14 million in guaranteed money in free agency before selecting __Carson Beck__ at No. 65, so Brissett is unlikely to get a hefty raise before the season. He ranked as the QB7 (19.9 FPG) from Week 6 through the end of the season, but he won’t drop back 45.8 times per game as he did last season. Brissett isn’t the easiest click in best ball drafts, even at this suppressed ADP (178, QB28). The Cards are likely to be out of postseason contention, and they’ll want to take a look at Beck during the best ball money-making weeks. Brissett is much more intriguing in 2-QB/Superflex redraft leagues if you want to punt your second-QB spot until the middle rounds of the draft and use Brissett until he eventually is benched later in the season. *(May 19)*

full_text:
How many of you reading this had Jaxon-Smith Njigba finishing as the top player in fantasy football at this time in 2025? If you did, please send proof and a resume to Fantasy Points, and we’ll be sure to consider you for employment.

We’re always on the lookout for the next fantasy football breakout star — in fact, our guy Ryan Heath [has his own article examining the latest personnel trends](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/season/2026/finding-the-next-jaxon-smith-njigba-playcaller-tendencies#/) in the NFL to see if we can identify the *next* JSN. We highly recommend you check that article out, because it gave us an idea for our latest in the Fantasy Points Brain Trust series!

Ryan (understandably) sat this one out, as his work speaks for itself, but we polled the rest of our staff on who they believe are some underrated candidates to finish first overall at their respective positions in 2026 fantasy football leagues.

\> The __Fantasy Points Brain Trust__ article series will recur throughout the 2026 off-season. Make sure to get all access with a [Fantasy Points subscription](https://www.fantasypoints.com/plans)!

2026 Fantasy Football Darkhorse Candidates to Finish #1 at Their Position
-------------------------------------------------------------------------

##### __DeVonta Smith__, WR, Philadelphia Eagles

\> __ADP:__ Round 3, WR13 (Underdog)

We’re all looking for this year’s Jaxon Smith-Njigba, whose career jumped to a new stratosphere after the Seahawks made him the focal point of the passing game following D.K. Metcalf’s trade to Pittsburgh. Smith is a logical candidate for a massive leap in 2026, as a third-round fantasy pick who’s about to become the #1 receiver in a run-centric offense.

The Eagles are ready to send A.J. Brown out of town once his cap hit drops from $43 million to $16.4 million on June 1. Smith is set to be the clear top option for the first time since his rookie season, a role that he’s ready for as a former Heisman Trophy winner playing next to Jaylen Waddle and John Metchie at Alabama. Brown leaves behind a 27.5% target share and a 35% first-read share from last season, and Smith could push to be a top one of the league’s top target earners. Smith averaged 6.7/79.7 receiving and 9.7 targets per game for 16.6 FPG in three non-Week 18 contests without Brown the last two seasons.

Smith will be asked to play more on the perimeter with rookie Makai Lemon operating as the primary slot WR, which is a good thing with Jalen Hurts at quarterback. Smith ran 58% of his routes from the slot last season, and just 16.3% of his Hurts’ attempts (74 of 454) were thrown over the middle of the field. The Eagles brought in Sean Mannion to reverse their offensive fortunes, and Smith could be a big beneficiary if Mannion can pull off what Klint Kubiak did in Seattle last season. *__\[Tom Brolley\]__*

##### __Jaylen Waddle__, WR, Denver Broncos

\> __ADP:__ Round 5, WR24 (Underdog)

Betting on Waddle is a bet on how you view him as a talent — for me, he’s capable of being an alpha. He proved it many times when Tyreek Hill went down, including in 2025, when Waddle was top-10 in both TPRR and YPRR post-Tyreek.

Then there’s the anatomy of what’s needed to reach the WR1 overall outcome (or close):

 If you want a dark horse top-5 fantasy WR — they/their team must have these traits: 80%+ Route Share (very few WRs do this now) 4K+ Team Pass Yards No Rookie or Sophomore QBs (correlates with the one above) These traits exist in ~90% of top-5 WR half-ppr finishers since 2021… — Zain Dhanani (@DhananiZain) May 12, 2026 

Over the past four years, the 14 WRs who broke into the Top 5 that weren’t already in it averaged a 2.44 YPRR the season prior, with a median prior finish of WR24. Jaylen Waddle posted a 2.42 YPRR in 2025 while finishing as WR23, and did it with an atrocious situation around him.

Then the draft capital and historic treatment of Sean Payton WR1s quells my concerns about anyone who thinks Waddle can’t clear 80%+ route share. The haul that they traded for him is not WR2 or rotational WR compensation. Courtland Sutton (a non-elite alpha) ran 81% routes in this exact system — so why would Waddle (a better player) suddenly drop below that?

Lastly, we have Bo Nix, who had an uninspiring 2025 with a 6.42 YPA and 6.02 ANY/A, but Tua Tagovailoa averaged 6.8 YPA in 2021 without a separator, then jumped to 8.87 the moment Tyreek arrived. Jalen Hurts saw a +0.8 YPA bump in his first year with A.J. Brown. Elite separators don't just absorb targets; they unlock the QB. Nix enters Year 3 having never played with a WR like this. Waddle was 12th in ASS amongst WRs in 2025 — he’s a separator. A 4,000+-yard season is on the table for Nix, who had 3,900+ in 2025, which will unlock Waddle.

Waddle checks every box from the tweet above: he'll get 80%+ routes, Denver should clear 4K+ passing, and Nix is in Year 3. Add in the lack of elite target competition, a top-tier OL, and Waddle’s knack for explosive plays, and we have a strong buy opportunity at cost with a high floor. *__\[Zain Dhanani\]__*

##### __Tucker Kraft__, TE, Green Bay Packers

\> __ADP:__ Round 7, TE5 (Underdog)

Is a guy a “darkhorse” to finish as the #1 overall player at his position when he — technically — did it last year? Well, Kraft is going off the board as the TE5 in most drafts, and that’s a price I’m willing to pay for someone who was tied atop the leaderboards with Trey McBride at 16.2 FPG (PPR) through seven games, until an early-November knee injury robbed him of the rest of his season.

The injury recovery for Kraft is, obviously, a huge factor, but the fact that it occurred in early November and had surgery nearly immediately means he’ll be 10 months post-op when the 2026 season kicks off, giving him a solid chance to be ready for Week 1. And when Kraft does return to the field, he’ll be part of a Packers offense that removed Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks from its extremely crowded target tree this offseason.

That’s good news for Kraft, because his 18.3% target share in those magical first seven games last season was significantly below that of McBride (26%), and much of Kraft’s damage came from big plays (an insane 15.6 YPR, 12.03 YPT, 2.71 YPRR) and touchdowns (6) over that span. It stands to reason that Kraft’s efficiency will take a hit — those numbers were positively Gronkian. But even a slight increase in volume could help offset some of that decline, and we already *know* this is a player who can put up monster fantasy numbers when given the opportunity.

 Best TE seasons by Yards per Target Over Expectation [min. 40 tgts, since 2023] 1. TUCKER KRAFT ('25) — 4.7 2. George Kittle ('24) — 4.2 3. TUCKER KRAFT ('24) — 3.9 4. Dalton Kincaid ('25) — 3.2 5. George Kittle ('23) — 3.0 6. Sam LaPorta ('25) — 2.9 7. TUCKER KRAFT ('23) — 2.3 pic.twitter.com/KhaqBphaQD — Fantasy Points Data (@FantasyPtsData) February 26, 2026 

Kraft is someone who made the entire Packer offense go in 2025, and in the current “TE revolution” landscape, I’m sure Matt LaFleur and Jordan Love are excited to get back to working with him in 2026, as part of a narrower target tree. *__\[Joe Dolan\]__*

##### __Christian Watson__, WR, Green Bay Packers

\> __ADP:__ Round 5, WR29 (Underdog)

I don’t know who would be happier with a Christian Watson WR1 overall finish — me, Tazim Wajid (his dad), or Ryan Heath. While this hypothetical scenario would be entertaining for our Twitter followers, this dark horse pick is grounded in more than wishful thinking.

Watson’s 2025 season, coming off an ACL tear, deserves more recognition. He ranked 4th in YPRR (2.67), 5th in YPR (17.5), and 6th in FP/RR (0.58). And among downfield threats (>15.0 aDOT), no receiver was more efficient: 18.2% Target Share (WR2), 0.122 1D/RR (WR1), and 0.58 FP/RR (WR1). That resulted in a 30.0% spike week rate (>18.0 Underdog points), 9th-best among all WRs.

Watson’s fantasy ceiling continues to rise with the departure of Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks, who combined for 128 targets in 2025 — including 21 in the red zone and 11 in the end zone. Green Bay’s receiver room has been perennially crowded, and those exits, paired with [Matt LaFleur's comments](https://x.com/ByRyanWood/status/2048165651668156862?s=20) on the offense’s new direction, suggest Watson can fit the mold of a genuine WR1.

That confidence is well-placed. Projecting a fully healthy Watson to lead this Packers’ offense in targets, receiving yards, and touchdowns in 2026 is well within reason — especially if Tucker Kraft’s [return is delayed](https://x.com/SleeperNFL/status/2051721341473280042?s=20). The last time Watson was fully healthy (the first half of the 2024 season), he ranked top-5 in average separation score (0.187) and route win rate (22.2%).

Team-level context only strengthens the argument. The Packers’ offense has ranked top-10 in EPA/Pass in every season since Jordan Love took over as the starting QB in 2023, and is more than capable of elevating its top receiver to league-winning production. At a WR29 price tag that hasn’t budged all offseason, Watson remains one of the most exploitable discounts on the board. *__\[Kyle Menton\]__*

__\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\___

I was all-in on Watson as my breakout player heading into 2024, and as mentioned above, he ranked top-5 in average separation score (0.187) and route win rate (22.2%) that season, and he posted a sick 21.4 YPR average. But it was a nightmarish and volatile year that ended in a torn ACL late in the season, so he was basically off my radar last summer.

Going back to his college days, his hands have been quite suspect, but immediately upon his return last season, I was fairly stunned by his improved hands and physicality at the catch point. He posted the best catch rate of his career (63.3%) while maintaining a high 17.5 YPR average. It didn’t take long for me to opine that he was truly “commanding the ball” in this offense, which is saying something because the Packers had a plethora of strong receiving options. He looked fantastic, and he did it against man (2.55 YPRR) and zone (2.87).

There are two fewer options now with Romeo Doubs and Dontayvion Wicks off the roster, and I get the sense that HC Matt LaFleur is finally ready to actually feature his best receivers, namely Watson, who is, by far, their best option at the “X” receiver spot. Watson won’t likely be a high-volume receiver on the 2026 Packers, but he was only 51st in the NFL last season in targets-per-routes-run, so his volume is set to rise on a thinned-out Packers’ receiving corps. He’ll need to play in 14+ games and get some luck if he’s to lead his position in fantasy points, but it’s doable based on his big-play potential and his TD upside. Watson has scored 20 TDs on only 133 career receptions, which is an excellent 15% TD rate, and it’s up to 17% if we remove his injury-plagued 2024 campaign.

He’ll need to post Davante Adams-like TD numbers, but Adams was the overall WR9 in scoring last year with only 60/789 receiving (13.2 YPR), and a healthy Watson should clear 70 receptions for 1200+ yards, giving him a legit chance to finish top-5 in total scoring. An overall WR1 season isn’t very realistic, but it’s within his range of possible outcomes if he can play all 17 games. *__\[John Hansen\]__*

##### __Chase Brown__, RB, Cincinnati Bengals

\> __ADP:__ Round 2, RB11 (Underdog)

For the 2nd year in a row, Chase Brown lands right around the 2-3 turn in bestball drafts: Just outside the top 10 RBs as RB11. At first glance, the price tag seems completely reasonable. A lot of fantasy managers are still licking their wounds from the brutal early-season showing that Brown had in 2025. From weeks 1-7, Brown averaged just 3.65 YPC (RB71), 44.7% Success Rate (60th), and just 14.1 Expected Fantasy Points per game (RB18).

So what makes Chase Brown a legitimate dark horse candidate for RB1?

Chase Brown flipped a switch in week 8 and beyond, even before Joe Burrow’s return from injury. From weeks 8-18, Chase Brown’s YPC ballooned up to 4.82, Success Rate up over 56%, and his expected fantasy points were the 3rd highest of any RB at 18.5 per game. This is the 2nd year in a row that we saw Chase Brown become a potential league winner heading into the fantasy playoffs.

The Bengals' offensive environment remains one of the most reliable bets in fantasy when healthy. Cincinnati refused to add any RB competition and almost completely overhauled its defense. This move boosts Chase Brown’s usage while leading and ensures he gets more work to bleed the clock rather than chase points, thereby enhancing the receivers' stats more than the RBs'. For example, when leading from weeks 8-18, Chase Brown ranked RB5 in XFP/G despite being only RB13 in attempts (60 carries). *__\[Zach Swails\]__*

##### __Kyler Murray__, QB, Minnesota Vikings

\> __ADP:__ Round 11, QB21 (Underdog)

Murray could be the darkest horse in the stable to finish at the top of the QB position in fantasy, but we’re chasing a dream scenario, and Murray checks some boxes that could lead him to fantasy greatness.

Landing in Minnesota presents arguably Murray’s best pass-catching corps in his time in the league — with Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jauan Jennings, and TJ Hockenson at Murray’s disposal. 2020 was the last time Murray had a comparable group of pass catchers, and he was able to set career highs in passing yards (3,971) and passing touchdowns (26).

On top of that, under Kevin O’Connell, the Vikings have ranked 2nd > 1st > 6th > 30th in passing yards and t-3rd > t-4th > 5th > 18th in passing touchdowns. O’Connell was able to achieve those numbers with the likes of Kirk Cousins, Josh Dobbs, and Nick Mullens while resurrecting the career of Sam Darnold before the bottom fell out with JJ McCarthy at the helm last season. I think it’s within the range of outcomes that O’Connell can pull a Darnold-like resurrection out of Murray and return this offense to a top-5 passing offense.

While Murray is likely not the pure passer that Cousins and Darnold are, he is far superior as a runner. With only Jordan Mason and a 33-year-old Aaron Jones in the backfield, there’s a path for Murray to produce one of his best rushing seasons.

Murray certainly has very long odds to produce a QB1 season, but I think he’s worth a shot with a Kevin O’Connell passing offense, combined with the most mobile QB of O’Connell’s tenure. *__\[Bill O’Brien\]__*
